parishNotes.[note a]: The sum of the tax bases may not total to the England figure due to rounding.
parishNotes.[note b]:
Council tax payers in the Charter Trustees for the City of Durham are spread across multiple parishes in Durham (there are a number of areas covered by both a parish and a Charter Trustee). The sum of the individual tax bases for Durham in the parish level data will not equal the Durham total in the local authority level table, where the taxbase has been adjusted by 24,500 to avoid double counting. 

The taxbase figures for England in the Summary Table 1 are also based on the local authority level totals, and so will also not match the sum of parish level data or equal the sum of the totals shown for Civil Parishes, Charter Trustees, and Temples which are based on the parish level data and will count properties affected in both categories.
parishNotes.[note c]: The aggregate of local precepts presented here may be different to the Local Authority total due to rounding.
parishNotes.[note d]: Not all local authorities have local precepting authorities within their area. This table only includes local authorities where there are local precepting authorities.
parishNotes.[note e]: Precept figures exclude localised council tax support.
parishNotes.[note f]: Group parishes are individual parishes that have been grouped for precepting purposes.
parishNotes.[note g]: In 2026-27, there are 24,500 council tax payers that are charged by the Charter Trustees for the City of Durham and another parish council. These have been included in the taxbase of both the Charter Trustee and the parish council. Therefore the sum of the taxbase for Durham and England using the parish level data will be different to the England and Local Authority aggregates.
parishNotes.[note h]: Band D amounts are as reported by local authorities, they represent the amounts that have been billed and may not necessarily exactly match the value of the precept divided by the tax base.
parishNotes.[note i]: This precept is negative because the district council collects rental income from parish land on behalf of the parish and distributes this back to residents as a reduction on their Council Tax.
parishNotes.[note j]: Bournemouth Charter Trustee and Poole Charter Trustee no longer exist and Bournemouth Town Council, Broadstone Town Council and Poole Town Council have formed in 2026-27.
parishNotes.[note k]: St Albans Parish Council has split into St Albans Parish Council and Deer Park Parish Council in 2026-27.
parishNotes.[r]: The 2022-23 to 2025-26 figures have been revised since the previous publication as a result of corrected data from North Kesteven District Council.

parishChanges: Parishes which no longer exist, new parishes, and renamed parishes in 2026-27

New parishes can be created in previously unparished areas, while parished areas can revert to being unparished. New parishes can also be created as a result of boundary changes; a parish can split to form two or more new parishes, or adjacent parishes can merge to form a single larger parish. For more information on this see:
This worksheet contains three tables, presented next to each other vertically with one blank row in between the tables.
Some cells refer to notes which can be found in the 'Notes' worksheet. A blank cell in the 'Notes' column indicates that there is no relevant note for the row.
